history.alt_text: A cleanly severed heavy-gauge residential copper electrical cable resting on a weathered concrete floor in sharp macro focus.
history.caption: The rising wholesale cost of essential materials like copper wire means the same repair budget buys fewer replacements.
history.title: Copper-Material-Cost-Squeeze

style_when: the story turns on one physical thing — a part, a material, a component, a document — and what that thing costs, contains or crosses a border is the news
prompt: An extreme close-up editorial macro photograph of a cleanly severed heavy-gauge residential copper electrical cable resting asymmetrically on a dusty, weathered concrete basement floor. 100mm macro lens, razor-sharp focal plane on the exposed, bright copper strands. Shallow depth of field, with the background falling away into soft slate grey shadows. Strong, soft directional daylight raking in from the upper left, catching the metallic sheen of the copper and the matte texture of the concrete. Fine film grain, moody editorial atmosphere, muted bone white and slate grey surroundings with the rich rust-copper standing out. No people, no text.
negative_prompt: text, letters, garbled numbers, watermark, logos, typography, people, faces, hands
rationale: The editorial macro treatment isolates a specific, tangible physical material—the copper cable driving a 23 percent cost increase—forcing the reader to confront the literal substance of the economic squeeze.
subject: a cleanly severed heavy-gauge residential copper electrical cable
core_thesis: Rising costs of home repair materials, particularly copper and steel, are outpacing overall spending growth, fundamentally shrinking the purchasing power of a homeowner's maintenance budget.
core_conflict: Rising material input costs versus flat retail spending and stagnant remodel permits.
composition: extreme close-up macro, hero object asymmetrically on the right third

title: The Repair Budget Squeeze
